A mixed-effects model writes each individual parameter as a population value plus a random
deviation and integrates the deviations out of the likelihood. Random effects are declared in the
`parfn`; `em()` fits the model. Example: theophylline, twelve subjects, one oral dose each.

```{r setup}
```

## Pharmacokinetic model

Depot, central compartment of volume $V$, clearance $\mathrm{Cl}$ (volume per time).

```{r reactions}
```

`em()` needs second derivatives: `derivMode` with `"forward-forward"` and the forward-over-reverse
directions.

```{r model}
```

## Theophylline data

One condition per subject; the condition table holds dose in mg and body weight.

```{r data}
```

```{r, fig.height = 3.5}
head(table)
plotData(data) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "time [h]", y = "concentration [mg/L]", color = "Subject")
```

## Random-effect formulas

`define()` starts the transformation as in [Setting up models](guide-model.html), `branch()`
copies it per table row, `insert()` sets dose, initial values and log parameters. Effect formulas
in lme4 notation give the linear predictors:

```{r trafo}
```

The formula acts after the log transformation: $\log \mathrm{Cl}_i = \mathrm{Cl} +
\eta_{\mathrm{Cl},i}$, $\eta_{\mathrm{Cl},i} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \omega_{\mathrm{Cl}}^2)$.
Further forms:

- `Cl ~ 1 + (1 | ID)`: random intercept per subject.
- `Cl ~ 1 + logWeight + (1 | ID)`: a covariate, fixed effect `Cl_logWeight` on a table column.
- `Ka + Cl ~ 1 + (1 | p | ID)`: random effects of `Ka` and `Cl` correlated (same ID `p`).
- `Cl ~ 1 + wt + (1 + dose | p | ID)`: a covariate and a random slope, correlated with the
  intercept.
- `Cl ~ 1 + (1 | ID) + (1 | ID:OCC)`: variability between subjects and between occasions.
- `Cl ~ 1 + (1 | gr(ID, dist = spikeSlab()))`: spike-and-slab instead of normal random effects.

Conditions of one group share the group random effects. The random effects of one ID form a block
with full covariance; `omega_<a>_<b>` are the entries of the Cholesky factor of the block, with
the log of the diagonal. Spike-and-slab and Dirichlet-process random effects:
[Sparse deviations](guide-sparse-deviations.html).

## Marginal likelihood

`em()` maximizes the likelihood of fixed effects, $\Omega$ and error parameters with the random
effects integrated out. It takes `normL2(data, g * x * p, errmodel = e)`, or `normT(..., df = 4)`
for Student-t residuals, and builds the prior from `randomEffects(p)`. `method`:

| method | use | reported $-2 \log L$ |
|---|---|---|
| `"focei"` | default, fast, Laplace's approximation at the modes | Laplace |
| `"quadrature"` | skewed posteriors, few random effects per group | quadrature |
| `"laplaceEM"` | EM on the Laplace approximation | quadrature of level $K + 2$ |
| `"saem"` | many random effects per group, non-Gaussian posteriors | quadrature of level $K + 2$ |

$K$ is the number of random effects of a group. Derivations:
[Methods > Marginal likelihood](methods-nlme.html#marginal-likelihood),
[Methods > EM algorithm](methods-nlme.html#em-algorithm).

## First-order conditional estimation (FOCEI)

Laplace's approximation at the mode of each group, [Methods > FOCEI](methods-nlme.html#focei).

### FOCEI fit

`init` holds the parameters other than random effects and effect-formula coefficients (those start
at 0); standard deviations start at `control$sd`.

```{r focei, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
chapter <- stored("results/guide-nlme.rds", "results/guide-nlme.R", envir = new.env())
obj <- normL2(data, g * x * p, errmodel = e)
# the model of the fit, which the saved result leaves out, from an evaluation at the estimates
model <- c("prdfn", "data", "errfn", "design")
fit <- chapter$fit
fit[model] <- em(obj, random, fit, control = list(trustControl = list(iterlim = 0), boundary = FALSE),
                 verbose = FALSE)[model]
```

The fit is loaded from `results/guide-nlme.rds`, computed by `results/guide-nlme.R`.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
summary(fit)
```

`omega_*` are log standard deviations here. Shrinkage near 1 means the data of a subject hardly
move the individual parameter.

`value` is $-2 \log L$; `valueNonmem` compares with the NONMEM `OBJ` (`NA` for `normT()`). The fit
holds `Omega`, `omega`, `random`, `etaModes`, `etaSE` and `shrinkage`. Methods: `coef()`, `vcov()`,
`confint()` (Wald or `method = "profile"`), `logLik()`, `AIC()`, `BIC()`, `anova()`, `predict()`,
`residuals()`, `simulate()` and the plots below.

### FOCEI settings

| entry of `control` | default | controls |
|---|---|---|
| `sd` | `0.3` | start of standard deviations not in `init` |
| `innerControl` | `rinit = 1`, `rmax = 10`, `iterlim = 30`, `steptol = 1e-8`, `mtol = 1e-12` | trust region of the modes |
| `trustControl` | `rinit = 1`, `rmax = 10`, `iterlim = 200`, `ftol = 1e-7`, `mtol = 1e-5` | trust region of population parameters |
| `derivMode` | `"forward-reverse"` | volume-term second derivatives, or `"forward-forward"` |
| `secondOrderCorrection` | `TRUE` | derivative of the volume term |

`"forward-forward"` needs models built with `derivMode = "forward-forward"`.
`secondOrderCorrection = FALSE` biases the estimates
([Methods > Volume term](methods-nlme.html#volume-term)). `fixed` holds parameters at given values,
`sparse = TRUE` uses sparse Hessians. The solver error must stay below the tolerances.
`em(cores = )`: [Remote computing](guide-remote-computing.html#threads-and-processes).

## Adaptive sparse-grid quadrature

`method = "quadrature"` starts from the FOCEI fit and integrates on a sparse grid around each group
mode; level $K$ is Laplace's approximation. A certificate flags groups whose posterior the grid
does not resolve. [Methods > Adaptive sparse-grid
quadrature](methods-nlme.html#adaptive-sparse-grid-quadrature).

| entry of `control$quadrature` | default | controls |
|---|---|---|
| `tol` | `0.1` | allowed change of $-2 \log L$ by the next level, split over groups; `Inf` keeps stage levels |
| `levels` | `K + 1` | stages; level `K + s` is exact for total degree `2 s + 1` |
| `maxLevel` | `K + 8` | highest level |
| `tolDecrement` | `1e-4` | Newton decrement that ends a stage |
| `maxEcmPerStage` | `10` | rebuilds per stage |
| `cm1Control`, `maxCm1Iter` | `rinit = 1`, `ftol = mtol = 1e-8`; `30` | `trust()` settings and iterations of a step |
| `pruneTol` | `Inf` | drop nodes with log weight this far below the largest |
| `certificate` | `points = 256`, `seed = 1` | importance-sampling check, `FALSE` skips |

The fit holds `stageTrace`, `etaCov` (posterior covariance per group) and `certificate`;
`plotTrace(fit)` draws the trace.

## Laplace EM

`method = "laplaceEM"`: expectation conditional maximization on the Laplace approximation,
reporting the quadrature of level $K + 2$, without certificate. `control$quadrature` takes `epsEcm`
(default `1e-5`), `maxEcm` (default 200) and `cm1Control`, `maxCm1Iter`, `pruneTol`, `maxLevel`.
[Methods > Laplace EM](methods-nlme.html#laplace-em).

## Stochastic approximation EM (SAEM)

`method = "saem"` samples the random effects from the posterior and averages over iterations after
a burn-in; `set.seed()` reproduces a fit. Value and standard errors come from the quadrature of
level $K + 2$. [Methods > SAEM](methods-nlme.html#saem).

| entry of `control$saem` | default | controls |
|---|---|---|
| `nBurnin`, `nEM` | `200`, `300` | most burn-in and averaging iterations |
| `nMcmc`, `nLaplace` | `3`, `3` | random-walk and independence steps per iteration |
| `laplaceEvery` | `5` | iterations between mode refreshes |
| `laplaceScale` | `1.5` | covariance factor of the independence proposal |
| `window` | `25` | iterations of drift test and averaging start |
| `mcTol` | `0.05` | Monte Carlo increase of $-2 \log L$ that ends averaging |

## Comparison of methods

The four methods from the same start:

```{r compare, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
fits <- list(focei = fit, quadrature = chapter$quadrature, saem = chapter$saem)
round(sapply(fits, function(f) c(f$argument[names(fit$argument)], minus2logL = f$value)), 3)
```

```{r laplaceem, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
laplaceEM <- chapter$laplaceEM
round(c(laplaceEM$argument[names(fit$argument)], minus2logL = laplaceEM$value), 3)
```

Estimates agree within their standard errors. FOCEI may lie below the quadrature: Laplace's method
is no bound.

```{r}
fits$quadrature$stageTrace[, c("level", "ecmIter", "OFV", "decrement", "resolution", "maxLevel", "nodes")]
fits$quadrature$certificate
```

`r q <- fits$quadrature$stageTrace; if (nrow(q) == 1 && q$decrement[1] < q$resolution[1]) "Here one rebuild ends the fit: the Newton decrement on the rebuilt nodes lies below what the nodes resolve, so the estimate of FOCEI stands, with the value of the quadrature." else sprintf("Here the fit takes %d rebuilds.", nrow(q))` `r flagged <- sum(fits$quadrature$certificate$flag); if (flagged == 0) "No group is flagged." else sprintf("%d of %d groups are flagged.", flagged, nrow(fits$quadrature$certificate))`

## Model diagnostics

Individual (IPRED, random effects at the modes) and population prediction (PRED, random effects 0):

```{r, fig.height = 6.5}
plotCombined(fit, ncol = 4) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "time [h]", y = "concentration [mg/L]")
```

Conditional weighted residuals (CWRES) linearize around the modes; normalized prediction
distribution errors (NPDE) come from simulations. Both should be standard normal.

```{r, fig.height = 6}
plotResiduals(fit, type = c("CWRES", "NPDE"), nsim = 200, seed = 1)
```

Visual predictive check:

```{r, fig.height = 3.5}
plotVPC(fit, nsim = 200, bins = 8, seed = 1)
```

Conditional draws of the random effects against the fitted $\mathcal{N}(0, \Omega_{kk})$:

```{r, fig.height = 5}
plotRandomEffects(fit)
```

Random effects against a covariate:

```{r, fig.height = 3.5}
plotRandomEffects(fit, covariates = table["weight"])
```

## Covariate effects

Body weight as a fixed effect on a table column, centered on log scale:

```{r covariates, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
fit2 <- chapter$fit2
comparison <- anova(fit, fit2)
comparison
```

`anova()` compares nested fits by likelihood ratio. Weight lowers $-2 \log L$ by
`r round(comparison$chisq[2], 2)`, p-value `r round(comparison$p[2], 2)`; the simpler model stays.

## Nested and crossed groups

Nested groupings (occasions within subjects) or crossed ones (patients and centers) are further
formula terms, integrated by FOCEI per connected component of the conditions. The
[pharmacometrics project](pharmacometrics.html) fits mavoglurant with between-occasion variability:

```r
insert(trafo, Cl ~ 1 + (1 | ID) + (1 | ID:OCC))
```

Which groups differ at all: [Sparse deviations](guide-sparse-deviations.html).


## Multistart optimization

`msem()` runs `em()` from `fits` starts, the first at `init`, the others perturbed with standard
deviation `sd`, and returns the best fit, all starts in `$multistart`. `theophyllineMultistart.R`
of the project `pharmacometrics` runs 200 starts each for FOCEI, quadrature and SAEM; the result is
loaded from `results/multistart.rds` of the project.

```{r, include = FALSE, purl = FALSE}
project <- normalizePath("../../examples/pharmacometrics")
knitr::read_chunk("../../examples/pharmacometrics/theophyllineMultistart.R")
```

```{r multistart, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
saved <- stored(file.path(project, "results", "multistart.rds"),
                file.path(project, "theophyllineMultistart.R"), envir = new.env())
values <- unlist(lapply(saved$multistart, `[[`, "value"))
wide <- diff(range(values, na.rm = TRUE)) > 50
lowest <- vapply(saved$multistart, function(t) sum(t$value < min(t$value, na.rm = TRUE) + 1, na.rm = TRUE), 0)
```

FOCEI:

```{r, fig.height = 3.5}
plotValues(saved$multistart$FOCEI, pseudoLog = wide)
```

Quadrature and SAEM, both valued by the quadrature:

```{r, fig.height = 3.5}
plotValues(saved$multistart[c("quadrature", "SAEM")], pseudoLog = wide)
```

All three methods find the same two optima. About `r round(mean(lowest))` of
`r nrow(saved$multistart[[1]])` starts per method reach the lower one, the flip-flop solution:

```{r}
flipflop <- saved$best$FOCEI
signif(rbind(fit = c(exp(fit$argument[c("Ka", "V", "Cl")]), minus2logL = fit$value),
             flipflop = c(exp(flipflop[c("Ka", "V", "Cl")]),
                          minus2logL = min(saved$multistart$FOCEI$value, na.rm = TRUE))), 4)
```

With one oral dose, absorption and elimination can swap: absorption becomes the slow step, the
volume shrinks to `r round(exp(flipflop[["V"]]), 1)` L and the `Ka` random effect vanishes. The
likelihood prefers it by `r round(fit$value - min(saved$multistart$FOCEI$value, na.rm = TRUE), 1)`,
but theophylline spreads through the body water, about 0.5 L/kg; a prior on `V` selects the upper
plateau.

### Zero variance components

A variance that runs to 0 is returned at 0 and named in `fit$boundary`; `control$boundary`
(default 0.1) is the accepted rise of $-2 \log L$, `FALSE` switches it off
([Methods > Zero variance components](methods-nlme.html#variance-at-the-boundary)). On the lower
plateau every method does so:

```{r}
sapply(saved$multistart, function(t) sum(t$boundary == "omega_Ka_Ka"))
sapply(saved$best, function(b) signif(b[c("Ka", "V", "Cl")], 4))
```

`theophyllineMultistart.R` refits the best fit of each method by every other method:

```{r crosscheck, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r}
saved$cross
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
byMethod <- split(saved$cross$value, saved$cross$by)
quadratureValue <- mean(byMethod$quadrature)
# a bound on the distance of SAEM to the quadrature, one significant digit
saemGap <- max(abs(byMethod$SAEM - quadratureValue))
saemGap <- ceiling(saemGap / 10^floor(log10(saemGap))) * 10^floor(log10(saemGap))
```

Each method reaches the same estimates from every start. FOCEI lies about
`r signif(quadratureValue - mean(byMethod$FOCEI), 2)` below the quadrature, SAEM within
`r saemGap` of it.

`msem()` draws all starts and seeds before spreading fits over `cores`, so `set.seed()` reproduces
a run; `cores = c(fits = , conditions = )`: see
[Remote computing](guide-remote-computing.html#threads-and-processes).

Reference: `randomEffects()`, `em()`, `msem()`, `anova()`, `plotResiduals()`, `plotVPC()`,
`plotRandomEffects()`, `plotTrace()`, `plotValues()`
